topic: December 2025 AILET Corner: Current Affairs Facts

subtopics.title: Polity, Law and Regulators
subtopics.summary: This subtopic covers the contempt of court framework in India, including the Court of Record status given to the Supreme Court and High Courts. It also covers the UMEED portal for Waqf properties and the Competition Commission of India's probe into airline flight disruptions.
facts: Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 governs contempt proceedings in India
Civil contempt: wilful disobedience of a judgment, decree, direction or order of a court
Criminal contempt: publication or act that scandalises or lowers the authority of a court
Criminal contempt also covers interfering with judicial proceedings and obstructing administration of justice
Article 129: Supreme Court is a Court of Record with power to punish for its own contempt
Article 215: High Courts enjoy similar Court of Record status with power to punish for contempt
UMEED stands for Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development under the Waqf Act, 1995
UMEED is a centralised digital platform for Waqf property management, monitoring and transparency
UMEED nodal agency: Ministry of Minority Affairs
CCI is a statutory body under the Competition Act, 2002; established in 2003
CCI took cognisance of IndiGo flight disruptions to probe possible abuse of dominant position

subtopics.title: Economy and Finance
subtopics.summary: This subtopic covers the RBI's regulation of Domestic Systemically Important Banks, the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2021 for customer grievances, and the Goldilocks economy after a repo rate cut. It also covers the Economic Census, which is conducted to build a business register and support planning.
facts: D-SIBs are referred to as 'Too Big To Fail'
D-SIBs are banks whose failure could trigger a significant disruption in the financial system and economy
D-SIBs are designated by the Reserve Bank of India
D-SIBs must maintain higher Common Equity Tier 1 (CET 1) capital than regular banks
Each D-SIB is placed in a risk bucket; a higher bucket means a higher additional CET 1 requirement
Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2021 merges the Banking (2006), NBFC (2018) and Digital Transactions (2019) ombudsman schemes
Ombudsman can direct regulated entities to pay up to 20 lakh as compensation for financial loss
Goldilocks economy: RBI cut the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.25%, an economy neither too hot nor too cold
Economic Census: first held in 1977; the next one is due in 2027, after the two-phase population census

subtopics.title: Environment, Science and Defence
subtopics.summary: This subtopic covers the CAFE fuel-efficiency norms and their phases, the UNEP Global Environment Outlook (GEO-7) report, and the ISRO launch of BlueBird Block-2. It also covers wetland additions to the Ramsar List and the Majuli river island.
facts: CAFE norms are notified under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001
CAFE objectives: reduce fuel consumption, lower CO2 emissions, curb air pollution and reduce oil import dependency
CAFE phases: Phase I 2017-18, Phase II 2022-23, Phase III 2027-32
UNEP released the 7th Global Environment Outlook (GEO-7), 'A Future We Choose'; HQ in Nairobi
Pollution is linked to 9 million deaths every year
ISRO's LVM3-M6 launched BlueBird Block-2 into Low Earth Orbit on a commercial mission for AST SpaceMobile (USA)
Indian Coast Guard inducted Samudra Pratap, an indigenous pollution control vessel
Majuli: Charaichung Royal Bird Sanctuary was established in 1633 by Ahom ruler Pratap Singha; Majuli is the world's largest river island
Siliserh Lake and Kopra Reservoir were added to the Ramsar List, taking India's total to 96 wetlands

subtopics.title: International Bodies and Conventions
subtopics.summary: This subtopic covers the US-led Pax Silica initiative, from which India is excluded, and SoLAR Phase II for solar irrigation. It also covers the Biological Weapons Convention, the UNESCO education convention, the Kimberley Process chair and the ADB.
facts: Pax Silica is a US-led strategic geo-economic and technology initiative; India is excluded from it
Pax Silica covers the entire silicon value chain, from critical minerals to chips, AI infrastructure and logistics
Pax Silica members: US, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Netherlands, UK, Israel, UAE and Australia
SoLAR (Solar Irrigation for Agricultural Resilience) Phase II covers India, Bangladesh, Kenya and Ethiopia
SoLAR Phase I (2019-2024) was implemented by IWMI (Colombo) and the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation
Biological Weapons Convention: opened for signature in 1972, entered into force in 1975, 189 member states
Biological Weapons Convention prohibits development, production, stockpiling and use of biological and toxin weapons
UNESCO Convention against Discrimination in Education was adopted in 1960; India has not ratified it
ADB was established in 1966 and is headquartered in Manila; it revised India's FY26 GDP growth forecast to 7.2%
India chairs the Kimberley Process from January 2026 to keep conflict diamonds out of global trade

quizzes.passage: Indian courts have long held a power to punish persons who disrespect them, and recent developments have brought this power back into focus. In a recent ruling, the Supreme Court stated that the power to punish for criminal contempt is not a personal shield for judges. The Court also stressed that judges have the authority to forgive an offender, and that forgiveness can be given alongside punishment. Contempt is generally divided into two broad categories, and each category protects the justice system in a different way. Separately, the government has moved to bring Waqf property records into a single digital system. A minister recently made an announcement about the registration of Waqf properties. The system, known as UMEED, is meant to make the management of Waqf properties more efficient and transparent. Meanwhile, the Competition Commission of India has started to examine a sudden disruption to airline services. The regulator is checking whether a dominant company has misused its market position, which is a matter covered by competition law. Such steps show how courts, regulators and ministries each shape the rules that citizens and companies must follow in everyday life. Each institution in these stories works within a defined legal framework, which is why the exact provisions matter.

quizzes.passage: Economic news in December 2025 focused on how stable the Indian economy looked and how the banking system is being watched more closely. The Reserve Bank of India, which decides monetary policy, recently reduced its key policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point. The central bank described the situation as a rare Goldilocks phase, a term that describes an economy in a balanced state. In such a phase, growth is steady, inflation is low, employment is high and the economy shows no sign of overheating or recession. Regulators have also taken steps to strengthen the largest banks. Some banks are so large and so closely connected with the rest of the system that their failure could disrupt the entire economy, so they must hold extra capital. For customers, the RBI's grievance system has been reorganised. A single integrated scheme now handles complaints against banks, non-banking finance companies and other regulated entities, with the aim of resolving disputes quickly, transparently and at low cost. Looking ahead, the government will conduct another Economic Census once the population census is complete, with the data expected to support a unified business register and better planning for enterprises across the country. Together, these measures show how monetary policy, banking regulation, consumer protection and statistics work as connected parts of the financial system.
